title.narrative: Providing Life-saving Assistance through Nutrition Response to Conflict-Affected Populations in Northeast Nigeria (Bama, Gwoza Ngala).

description.narrative: ltpgtProviding Life-Saving Assistance through Nutrition and Protection Mainstreaming Response to Conflict-Affected Populations in Northeast Nigeria (Bama, Gwoza, and Ngala LGAs) of Borno state.ltbrgtThe protracted humanitarian crisis in Borno State continues to endanger the lives and well-being of conflict-affected populations, particularly internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, and vulnerable host communities in Bama, Gwoza, and Ngala LGAs. Years of armed conflict have disrupted health and nutrition systems, restricted access to essential services, and increased food insecurity. Children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLWs) remain at heightened risk of acute malnutrition, while exposure to protection risks continues to undermine recovery efforts.ltbrgtIn response to these persistent needs, the Concern for Women and Children Development Foundation (COWACDI) is implementing an integrated Nutrition and Protection Mainstreaming Project designed to strengthen community-based preventive nutrition services and referral mechanisms for timely access to treatment. The intervention aims to reduce morbidity and mortality linked to acute malnutrition and ensure that vulnerable groups access humanitarian assistance in a safe, dignified, and inclusive manner.ltbrgtThe nutrition component will focus on:ltbrgtCommunity-Level Active Case Finding: Conducting household visits and community screening using Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) to identify children with Moderate and Severe Acute Malnutrition.ltbrgtReferral and Linkage to Treatment Services: Strengthening referral pathways to Outpatient Therapeutic Programmes (OTPs), Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programmes (TSFPs), and Stabilization Centres (SCs) managed by partners and government facilities.ltbrgtMaternal, Infant, and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN): Conducting community counselling sessions on exclusive breastfeeding, complementary feeding, and maternal dietary practices.ltbrgtMicronutrient Supplementation and Awareness: Supporting community sensitisation and mobilisation during Vitamin A and deworming campaigns to improve child nutrition outcomes.ltbrgtCommunity Engagement and Behavioural Change: Using cooking demonstrations and nutrition education sessions to promote locally available, nutrient-rich diets such as the Tom Brown approach for MAM management at household level.ltbrgtThe protection mainstreaming strategy will ensure all nutrition activities uphold the principles of safety, dignity, inclusivity, and accountability. COWACDI will:ltbrgtIntegrate safeguarding and protection from sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) such as training for all staff and community volunteers.ltbrgtEstablish safe and accessible referral pathways for individuals at risk of violence, neglect, or abuse.ltbrgtPromote equal participation of women, men, and persons with disabilities in community nutrition sessions.ltbrgtFacilitate community feedback and complaint mechanisms to strengthen accountability to affected populations.ltbrgtEnsure service delivery is gender-sensitive and culturally appropriate to local norms.ltbrgtImplementation will leverage trained community volunteers, existing community structures, and collaboration with Primary Health Care Centres (PHCs), Local Government Authorities, and the Borno State Primary Health Care Development Agency (BSPHCDA). This community-driven approach ensures sustainability, strengthens local ownership, and aligns with state and sector coordination frameworks.ltbrgtWith a total budget of $150,000 and a population target of 11,042 direct beneficiaries, this project will improve early detection and referral of malnutrition cases, enhance preventive nutrition practices, and integrate protection considerations into all stages of programming. Through this initiative, COWACDI seeks to safeguard the well-being of conflict-affected populations while promoting equitable access to essential nutrition services in Northeast Nigeria.ltbrgtlt/pgt
